subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A 4-bit binary number is shifted left by 1 place, but the leftmost 1 is lost. What error has occurred?
questions.explain: Losing the most significant bit during a left shift causes an overflow because the result no longer fits.

questions.q: During the fetch stage, which register holds the address of the NEXT instruction to be fetched?
questions.explain: The Program Counter stores the address of the next instruction to be fetched and is incremented each cycle.

questions.q: Which formula gives the file size of an uncompressed bitmap image (ignoring metadata)?
options: width x height x colour depth (in bits)
questions.explain: Image file size in bits is the number of pixels (width x height) multiplied by the colour depth.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the von Neumann architecture?
options: Program instructions and data are stored in the same memory
Programs are stored permanently in the ALU
The CPU has no need for any registers
Instructions and data are stored in physically separate memories
questions.explain: In the von Neumann architecture a single shared memory holds both program instructions and the data they operate on.

questions.q: What effect does a logical left shift of 1 place have on an unsigned binary number?
options: It has no effect on the value
questions.explain: Each left shift of one place multiplies an unsigned binary number by 2.

questions.q: When data is fetched from RAM during the cycle, which register does it arrive in?
questions.explain: The Memory Data Register holds the data or instruction transferred to or from memory.

questions.q: A black-and-white (1 bit per pixel) image is 10 pixels wide and 8 pixels high. What is its size in bytes, ignoring metadata?
questions.explain: 10 x 8 = 80 bits, and 80 / 8 = 10 bytes.

questions.q: Increasing which of the following would most directly allow a CPU to execute more instructions per second?
options: The size of the hard drive
questions.explain: A higher clock speed means more fetch-decode-execute cycles are completed each second.

questions.q: When adding the 8-bit binary numbers 11111111 and 00000001, what occurs?
options: The numbers cannot be added in binary
The result fits exactly in 8 bits with no issue
An overflow occurs because the result needs a 9th bit
questions.explain: 11111111 + 00000001 = 100000000, which needs 9 bits, so an overflow error occurs in an 8-bit register.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the fetch-decode-execute cycle?
questions.explain: The CPU first fetches an instruction from memory, decodes what it means, then executes it.

questions.q: Why is hexadecimal often used by programmers instead of long binary numbers?
options: Hexadecimal can represent numbers that binary cannot
It is shorter and easier for humans to read and less error-prone than binary
It uses only the digits 0 and 1
Computers store data directly in hexadecimal
questions.explain: Hex is a more compact, human-friendly way to write binary, as each hex digit maps to exactly 4 bits.

questions.q: What does the term 'metadata' mean when applied to an image file?
options: The actual colour value of each individual pixel
The compression algorithm running on the file
The sample rate of the image
Extra data stored about the image, such as its dimensions and date created
questions.explain: Metadata is data about the file, such as resolution, colour depth and creation date.

questions.q: What is the 8-bit binary representation of the denary number 200?
What is the purpose of the Accumulator (ACC) in the CPU?
options: To store the operating system permanently
To temporarily store the results of calculations from the ALU
To hold the address of the memory being accessed
To store the address of the next instruction
questions.explain: The Accumulator temporarily holds the intermediate results of arithmetic and logic operations.

questions.q: Which secondary storage type uses spinning platters and read/write heads to store data magnetically?
questions.explain: A magnetic hard disk drive stores data on spinning platters that are magnetised by read/write heads.

questions.q: How many different values can be represented using 4 bits?
questions.explain: 4 bits give 2 to the power 4 = 16 different combinations.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of system software?
questions.explain: The operating system is system software that manages the computer's hardware and resources, unlike application software.

questions.q: Which statement about ROM is correct?
options: It is volatile and loses its contents when switched off
It is non-volatile and typically holds the boot/start-up instructions
It can be easily rewritten thousands of times during normal use
It is used as the computer's main working memory
questions.explain: ROM is non-volatile and usually stores the start-up (boot) instructions the computer needs when first switched on.

questions.q: A larger CPU cache generally improves performance because it:
options: Reduces how often the CPU must wait for data from slower RAM
Increases the amount of secondary storage
questions.explain: A bigger cache lets more frequently used data sit close to the CPU, reducing waits for slower RAM.

questions.q: What is the denary (decimal) value of the binary number 00101101?
In a bitmap image, what does increasing the colour depth (bits per pixel) allow?
options: A greater number of possible colours per pixel
A larger number of pixels in the image
questions.explain: Colour depth is the number of bits used per pixel, so more bits means more possible colours.

questions.q: Which is a key advantage of a solid state drive (SSD) over a magnetic hard disk drive?
options: It always has a larger storage capacity
It is always cheaper per gigabyte
It has no moving parts, so it is faster and more durable
It is volatile and so loses data quickly
questions.explain: SSDs have no moving parts, making them faster and more shock-resistant than magnetic drives.
